summary: Throttling observed after tier promotion: fractional burst credits and priority-lane isolation mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a surge of 429 rejections after an account promotion from 'dedicated' to 'enterprise' (automatic quota refill/credit bump). The spikes began during an overnight bulk embedding job and persisted for ~45 minutes despite apparent console credit increase.

Impact:
- NimbusSearch ingestion pipeline experienced ~28% failed requests resulting in degraded indexing throughput.
- Customer on enterprise plan; observed throttles during their SLA window.

Environment:
- Account: NimbusSearch Inc (enterprise)
- Region: us-west-2 (dedicated GPU pool)
- Models: redwood-open-7b-v1 pinned
- Traffic shape: mixed short-lived streaming sessions for product search + large parallel embedding upload workers (100+ concurrent connections)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Promote account via console (billing tier change) at 02:10 UTC.
2) Kick off nightly embedding backfill at 02:30 UTC using 120 workers multiplexing signed URLs.
3) Observe intermittent 429s logged by client at 02:35-03:15 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows immediate credit bump at 02:11 UTC.
- Request traces show early rejections with throttle_reason: TOKEN_WINDOW_DEPLETED and throttle_type: route_isolation.
- Throttle headers include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 for many connections.
- Some healthcheck probes and a legacy background archiver were still being counted against the tenant burst pool.

Expected behavior:
- Promotion should reconcile burst credits and ensure priority-lane allocation for enterprise background vs realtime lanes. Background workers should be isolated or deprioritized to avoid interactive stream rejections.

Additional notes:
- Customer included a sample log bundle and pcap of connection attempts.
- They observed a slow console refresh (UI shows new credits but API-layer refill epoch lagged).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Promote tenant; 2) Run concurrent embedding workers with signed-url callback fanout; 3) Monitor for 429s in client logs and X-RateLimit headers
comments: 2026-03-10 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer requested urgent help. Attached logs and sample trace IDs. Asked for initial triage and whether this is known during promotions.

2026-03-10 12:05 - Tomas Rivera: Started triage. Checked control-plane events and saw tier-change event at 02:10 UTC. Console credit metric shows +500k tokens at 02:11 but rate-limiter refill metric (rls_refill_epoch) shows next epoch at 02:30. Possible refill epoch misalignment.

2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE Team (note): Observed background archiver service (svc-archiver-legacy) sending constant keepalive probes which were counted against the tenant burst pool. Filed INT-330 to coordinate excluding internal probes.

2026-03-10 15:10 - Tomas Rivera: Reproduced locally with a scaled test harness. When promotion occurs mid-window the per-route fractional-burst-credit calculation sometimes uses pre-promotion burst-share snapshot leading to temporary negative effective credits on small route shards.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Customer (NimbusSearch): Confirmed temporary mitigation by staggering promotion outside their backfill window reduced rejections. Asked for concrete config changes so this won't recur on future tier transitions.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Refill epoch alignment: control-plane updates console balance immediately but rate-limiter applies credits at discrete refill epochs resulting in temporal mismatch.
- Fractional/route-level accounting: when tenant burst credit increases the shard allocation uses a cached snapshot for a short interval; large concurrent fanout can exhaust per-route fractional shares before global refill sync.
- Healthcheck/internal probes consuming burst: legacy archiver and some k8s readiness probes counted against same pool.

Checks performed:
- Verified billing/promotion event at 02:10 UTC in ledger (ledger_txn_78910).
- Pulled rls_refill_epoch metrics and token_bucket levels for tenant: gap observed between 02:11 and first post-update epoch at 02:30.
- Looked at edge-proxy logs: many signed-url callbacks reusing pooled IPs; connection reuse may have increased per-connection route accounting.

Partial findings:
- Confirmed temporal window where console balance != rate-limiter effective usable credits.
- Found that per-route fractional allocation algorithm uses integer rounding down which can cause small routes to appear zeroed if global credits jump mid-epoch.
- Healthcheck probes contributed ~4% of traffic during the spike but were enough to push some route shards below usable threshold given high fanout.
workaround:
1) Recommend customer delay promotions until after large backfills or schedule staggered worker startup.
2) Short-term: temporarily throttle background archiver or exclude its IPs from tenant burst accounting via ACL (we coordinated with SRE to whitelist healthcheck IPs for this customer).
3) Enable 'grace-refill' flag on tenant (internal feature flag) to apply an immediate provisional refill for up to one epoch to smooth the promotion transition.
resolution_notes:
Root cause: refill-epoch mismatch combined with per-route fractional rounding and background probe accounting.
Fixes applied:
- Rolled out a control-plane patch to trigger a provisional refill event on tier-change to avoid a full epoch wait (deploy id: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/commit/ab12ef).
- Adjusted fractional allocation algorithm to use stochastic rounding instead of floor for small route shares (deploy id: github.com/redwood-inference/rls/commit/d3c9aa).
- SRE whitelisted internal archiver probes for NimbusSearch to prevent background probe accounting against burst pool.

Status: Patch deployed to prod-us-west on 2026-03-11 04:25 UTC. Customer verified that a simulated promotion + backfill no longer produced 429s. Follow-up: monitor tenant metrics for 72 hours and schedule a postmortem runbook update.
postmortem_followup:
- Update runbook 'tier-promotion-checklist' with steps to schedule promotions and enabling grace-refill.
- Create dashboard that alerts when console_balance != rls_refill_effective for >1 minute.
- Recommend product add UI notice when promotions occur in active windows.
- Owner: Tomas Rivera; due: 2026-03-20
external_communication: 2026-03-11 06:00 - Aisha Patel to NimbusSearch: Provided mitigation steps, confirmed patch rollout, and requested permission to monitor for 72 hours. Customer accepted and will report any regressions.
notes_for_engineering: Prioritize a small test that performs tier-change during high-fanout jobs and verify provisional-refill behavior. Validate stochastic rounding under extreme shard counts (10k+ routes). Also consider designing a transient 'credit-burst' state for promotions.
customer_impact_summary: Temporary ingestion failures (~28% of requests) for ~45 minutes during promotion; mitigation reduced impact and long-term fix deployed. Customer satisfied with workaround and patch.
